{{Short description|Proposal concerning the state of the universe prior to the Planck epoch}}

[[File:Big Bang Singularity and Hartle-Hawking State.jpg|thumb|400x400px|Comparison of the [[Big Bang]] concept (left) and a Hartle–Hawking state concept (right) as they are extrapolated to time zero. Diagram shows two space dimensions horizontally and one time dimension vertically.<ref name=open-inflation>{{Cite web |title=Centre for Theoretical Cosmology: The Origins of the Universe: General open inflation |url=https://www.ctc.cam.ac.uk/outreach/origins/inflation_four.php |access-date=2025-08-23 |website=www.ctc.cam.ac.uk}}</ref>]]

The '''Hartle–Hawking state''', also known as the '''no-boundary wave function''', is a [[cosmological]] model that applies [[quantum mechanics]] to the [[Big Bang]].<ref name=Penrose-2005/>{{rp|769}}
It is named after [[James Hartle]] and [[Stephen Hawking]], who first proposed it in 1983.<ref name="Hartle-Hawking">{{Cite journal |last1=Hartle |first1=J. |last2=Hawking |first2=S. |year=1983 |title=Wave function of the Universe |journal=Physical Review D |volume=28 |issue=12 |pages=2960 |bibcode=1983PhRvD..28.2960H |doi=10.1103/PhysRevD.28.2960 |s2cid=121947045}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Lehners|first=Jean-Luc|date=June 2023|title=Review of the no-boundary wave function|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0370157323001904|journal=Physics Reports|language=en|volume=1022|pages=1–82|doi=10.1016/j.physrep.2023.06.002|arxiv=2303.08802 |bibcode=2023PhR..1022....1L }}</ref>
The concept can also be considered as an initial condition for models of [[quantum cosmology]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Weinberg|first=Steven|date=1989-01-01|title=The cosmological constant problem|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1|journal=Reviews of Modern Physics|language=en|volume=61|issue=1|pages=1–23|doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.61.1|bibcode=1989RvMP...61....1W |hdl=2152/61094|issn=0034-6861|hdl-access=free}}</ref>{{rp|14}} 

== Ingredients ==
The Hartle-Hawking proposal includes several ingredients. First it uses [[Richard Feynman]]'s [[path integral formulation]] of quantum mechanics. In this approach every possible path a particle can take through spacetime contributes to the solution with its own amplitude and phase. Technical challenges with those sums lead to the second ingredient, a transformation to [[Euclidean space|Euclidean]] space-time: a geometry which combines 3 space dimensions with an imaginary time dimension.<ref name=HawkingBrief-1996/>{{rp|172}} This is related to the [[Wick rotation]], <math>\tau = it</math>, and it converts the spacetime metric in to a Euclidean metric, <math>ds^2 = d\tau^2 + dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2</math>. In Hawking's approach, this rotation is applied to every path, not to the background space of the paths as in Wick's approach, and therefore the sum of histories becomes a quantum superposition of spacetimes.<ref name=Penrose-2005/>{{rp|769}} This curved Euclidean spacetime can be analogous to a sphere in being both finite in extent and yet have no boundary.<ref name=HawkingBrief-1996/>{{rp|174}}

== History ==
The original 1983 paper by Hartle and Hawking grew out of a summer visit by Hawking to [[UC Santa Barbara]] where Hartle worked. Hawking was exploring the idea that the boundary condition for space time was simply no-boundary at all.
With Hartle this idea was converted in to a proposal and published.<ref name=HawkingBrief-1996>{{Cite book |last=Hawking |first=Stephen |title=The illustrated A brief history of time |date=1996 |publisher=Bantam Books |isbn=978-0-553-10374-8 |edition=Updated and expanded |location=New York}}</ref>{{rp|175}}
In 1998 Hawking worked with Neil Turok to expand the Hartle-Hawking concept to include a [[Shape of the universe|hyperbolic]] or open geometry.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hawking |first1=S. W. |last2=Turok |first2=Neil |date=1998 |title=Open inflation without false vacua |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269398002342 |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=425 |issue=1 |pages=25–32 |doi=10.1016/S0370-2693(98)00234-2 |arxiv=hep-th/9802030 |bibcode=1998PhLB..425...25H |issn=0370-2693}}</ref><ref name=Penrose-2005>{{Cite book |last=Penrose |first=Roger |title=The road to reality: a complete guide to the laws of the universe |date=2005 |publisher=A.A. Knopf |isbn=978-0-679-45443-4 |edition=1st American |location=New York}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hawking |first1=S. W. |last2=Turok |first2=Neil |date=April 16, 1998 |title=Open inflation without false vacua |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0370269398002342 |journal=Physics Letters B |volume=425 |issue=1 |pages=25–32 |doi=10.1016/S0370-2693(98)00234-2 |arxiv=hep-th/9802030 |bibcode=1998PhLB..425...25H |issn=0370-2693}}</ref><ref name=open-inflation/>
